newsitem.title: USA: Cell Genesys, Somatix to merge.
newsitem.headline: Cell Genesys, Somatix to merge.

text.p: Two small companies involved in cutting-edge gene research Monday announced an $82.8 million merger, saying the combination would help bring a new generation of AIDS and cancer drugs to the market.
Cell Genesys Inc. and Somatix Therapy Corp. said that by pooling their resources they would create the leading company in gene therapy.
The field has emerged as one of the hottest areas of drug research in recent years amid dramatic advances in genetic research.
While none of the scores of companies to enter the field of gene therapy have yet turned their research into a commercial drug, Cell Genesys and Somatix are relatively far along in their efforts.

Cell Genesys, based in Foster City, Calif., is conducting a human clinical trial of an AIDS drug, and plans later this month to report interim results. The strategy is based on collecting a patient's T cells -- part of the immune system -- genetically modifying them so they can detroy HIV-infected cells, and then reinjecting them into the patient. The company is pursuing similar research to treat cancer.

Alameda, Calif.-based Somatix has developed a cancer vaccine which will enter clinical trials for lung cancer later this year. It has similar treatments for Parkinson's disease and hemophilia in development.
Cell Genesys Chairman Stephen Sherwin, who will head the newly merged company, said in an interview that he expected the company's first drugs to come on the market in 2001 or 2002.

While researchers have not yet figured out how to safely and effectively deliver such treatments to a patient, they say the potential payoff is worth the lengthy development time, especially in diseases like cancer, where existing treatments are highly toxic. New gene-based cancer drugs could potentially allow patients to avoid the severe side effects of chemotherapy.

Under the merger agreement, Somatix will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Cell Genesys through a stock exchange of 0.385 shares of Cell Genesys for each Somatix share held. Based on Somatix' 24.4 million shares outstanding, the deal is valued at $82.8 million.

"Gene therapy offers extraordinary opportunities to intervene at the most basic levels of the disease process and apply our increasing knowledge of the relationship of genes to disease," Sherwin said in a statement.

He said the merger would create a "gene therapy powerhouse" in terms of talent, intellectual property and commercial opportunties. Because the two companies have explored different methods of gene drug delivery, certain advantages would result from the merger, he said.

Cell Genesys has emphasized so called ex vivo research in which a patient's cells are removed, genetically altered and then reintroduced. Somatix has focused on in-vivo techinques in which genes found to have disease-fighting properties are introduced into the body.
